Glossary of Islam.fact: In theology, it is the one-way barrier between the mortal realm and the spirit world which the deceased soul crosses and waits for Qiyamah judgment.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Baṣīrah (بصيرة) _____, discernment, perceptivity, deep knowledge
Glossary of Islam.fact: Baṣīrah (بصيرة) Insight, discernment, perceptivity, deep knowledge.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Sometimes used by _____ to denote the ability to directly perceive a transcendental Truth
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sometimes used by Sufis to denote the ability to directly perceive a transcendental Truth.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: (والسلام) Blessed be _____, an acronym for S.A.W.S
Glossary of Islam.fact: (والسلام) Blessed be His Name, an acronym for S.A.W.S. Bidʿah (بدعة) Innovation in religion, i.e.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Bidʿah (بدعة) _____ in religion, i.e
Glossary of Islam.fact: (والسلام) Blessed be His Name, an acronym for S.A.W.S. Bidʿah (بدعة) Innovation in religion, i.e.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Bidʿah sayyiʾah (سيئة) _____ prohibited in Islam
Glossary of Islam.fact: Bidʿah sayyiʾah (سيئة) Inquiry prohibited in Islam.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Bismi-llāhi r-raḥmāni r-raḥīmi (بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم) "In the name of Allah, the _____, the Most Merciful"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Bismi-llāhi r-raḥmāni r-raḥīmi (بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم) "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Also called the _____, it is the phrase that is written or recited before each surah (except for the 9th surah, At-Tawbah)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Also called the Basmala, it is the phrase that is written or recited before each surah (except for the 9th surah, At-Tawbah).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: A specific reference is to the "burda" of Muḥammad (see Al-_____)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Burda (بردة) In general terms, it means a "cloak" or an "outer garment". A specific reference is to the "burda" of Muḥammad (see Al-Burda).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Bayʿah (بيعة) An oath of allegiance to a leader, traditionally the _____, a Sheikh or an Imam
Glossary of Islam.fact: Bayʿah (بيعة) An oath of allegiance to a leader, traditionally the Caliph, a Sheikh or an Imam.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Dajjāl (ٱلدَّجَّالُ) _____ equivalent of the Antichrist; meaning "liar" or "deceiver"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Dajjāl (ٱلدَّجَّالُ) The Islamic equivalent of the Antichrist; meaning "liar" or "deceiver".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḍallāl (ضلال) _____ astray
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḍallāl (ضلال) Going astray.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Dār al-ʿAhd (دَارُ الْعَهْدِ) _____'s relationship with its Christian tributary states
Glossary of Islam.fact: Dār al-ʿAhd (دَارُ الْعَهْدِ) The Ottoman Empire's relationship with its Christian tributary states.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Dār al-ʾAmn (دَارُ الْأَمْنِ) _____ a "house of safety"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Dajjāl (ٱلدَّجَّالُ) The Islamic equivalent of the Antichrist; meaning "liar" or "deceiver". Dār al-ʾAmn (دَارُ الْأَمْنِ) Meaning a "house of safety".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Dār al-ḥarb (دَارُ الْحَرْبِ) "House of war"; refers to areas outside _____ rule which a Muslim state can go to war with
Glossary of Islam.fact: Dār al-ḥarb (دَارُ الْحَرْبِ) "House of war"; refers to areas outside Muslim rule which a Muslim state can go to war with. Dār al-Islām (دَارُ الْإِسْلَامِ) "Home of peace." A country ruled by Islamic Law (see: Shari'ah), where both Muslims and non-Muslims (see: dhimam) practice religious tolerance.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Dār al-Islām (دَارُ الْإِسْلَامِ) "Home of peace." A country ruled by _____ (see: Shari'ah), where both Muslims and non-Muslims (see: dhimam) practice religious tolerance
Glossary of Islam.fact: Dār al-Islām (دَارُ الْإِسْلَامِ) "Home of peace." A country ruled by Islamic Law (see: Shari'ah), where both Muslims and non-Muslims (see: dhimam) practice religious tolerance.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Dār aṣ-Ṣulḥ (دَارُ الصُّلْحِ) "_____ of agreement"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Dār aṣ-Ṣulḥ (دَارُ الصُّلْحِ) "Domain of agreement".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Dār ash-shahāda (دَارُ الشَّهَادَةِ) See: Dar al-_____ūd (الدرود، الصلاة على النبي) "Blessing"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Dār ash-shahāda (دَارُ الشَّهَادَةِ) See: Dar al-Amn Darūd (الدرود، الصلاة على النبي) "Blessing".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Darwīš (درويش) An initiate of the _____, one who practices Sufism Dhikr (ذكر) A devotional practice whereby the name of God is repeated in a rhythmical manner
Glossary of Islam.fact: Darwīš (درويش) An initiate of the Sufi Path, one who practices Sufism Dhikr (ذكر) A devotional practice whereby the name of God is repeated in a rhythmical manner.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: A remembrance of God; a spiritual exercise; _____ believe that the primary function of prophets is to remind people of God
Glossary of Islam.fact: A remembrance of God; a spiritual exercise; Muslims believe that the primary function of prophets is to remind people of God. dhimam) "Protected person"; refers to Jews and Christians (and sometimes others, such as Buddhists, Sikhs, Hindus, and Zoroastrians) living in an Islamic state who must pay a separate tax (jizya) instead of the zakah paid by Muslims, exempting non-Muslims from military service under Islamic law.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Dīn (الدين) _____: "religion", the way of life based on Islamic revelation; the sum of a Muslim's faith and practice
Glossary of Islam.fact: Dīn (الدين) Literally: "religion", the way of life based on Islamic revelation; the sum of a Muslim's faith and practice.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Diyyah (دية) "_____ money", recompense for loss of a life
Glossary of Islam.fact: Diyyah (دية) "Blood money", recompense for loss of a life.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Div (دیو) "Demon", hideous creatures in _____ beliefs
Glossary of Islam.fact: Dīn (الدين) Literally: "religion", the way of life based on Islamic revelation; the sum of a Muslim's faith and practice. Div (دیو) "Demon", hideous creatures in Islamic beliefs.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Duʿāʾ (دعاء) _____ prayer, supplication
Glossary of Islam.fact: Duʿāʾ (دعاء) Personal prayer, supplication.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Dunya (دنيا) The physical _____ as opposed to the Hereafter; sometimes spelled Dunia
Glossary of Islam.fact: Dunya (دنيا) The physical Universe as opposed to the Hereafter; sometimes spelled Dunia.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Eid al-_____ the willingness of Ibrahim (Abraham) to sacrifice his son Ishmael (Isma'il) as an act of obedience to God's command
Glossary of Islam.fact: Eid al-Adha Honours the willingness of Ibrahim (Abraham) to sacrifice his son Ishmael (Isma'il) as an act of obedience to God's command.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Fajarah (فجرة) (also fujjār (فجّار)) _____ evil doers
Glossary of Islam.fact: Fajarah (فجرة) (also fujjār (فجّار)) Wicked evil doers.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: fajr (فجر) _____, early morning, and the morning prayer
Glossary of Islam.fact: fajr (فجر) Dawn, early morning, and the morning prayer.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Falāḥ (فلاح) _____, salvation, well-being
Glossary of Islam.fact: Falāḥ (فلاح) Deliverance, salvation, well-being.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Falsafah (فلسفة) "_____", the methods and content of Greek philosophy which were brought into Islam
Glossary of Islam.fact: Falsafah (فلسفة) "Philosophy", the methods and content of Greek philosophy which were brought into Islam. A person who tries to interpret Islam through rationalist philosophy was called a faylasuf (فيلسوف), English: "philosopher".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: A person who tries to interpret Islam through rationalist philosophy was called a faylasuf (فيلسوف), _____: "philosopher"
Glossary of Islam.fact: A person who tries to interpret Islam through rationalist philosophy was called a faylasuf (فيلسوف), English: "philosopher".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Fanā' (فناء) A _____ term meaning extinction, a spiritual death of the lower self (Nafs) with associated bad characteristics
Glossary of Islam.fact: Fanā' (فناء) A Sufi term meaning extinction, a spiritual death of the lower self (Nafs) with associated bad characteristics.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Al-_____ (الفرج) The return of the Shi'a Mahdi
Glossary of Islam.fact: Al-Faraj (الفرج) The return of the Shi'a Mahdi.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Neglecting a fard will result in a punishment in the _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: Neglecting a fard will result in a punishment in the Hereafter.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Farḍ ʿain ( عين) _____ on every individual Muslim to aid in any way they can
Glossary of Islam.fact: Farḍ (فرض), plural furūḍ (فروض) A religious duty, or an obligatory action: for example, praying 5 times a day is fard. Farḍ ʿain ( عين) Obligatory on every individual Muslim to aid in any way they can.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Farḍ kifāyah (كفاية) An obligation on the _____ community as a whole, from which some are freed if others take it up, such as for jihad
Glossary of Islam.fact: Farḍ ʿain ( عين) Obligatory on every individual Muslim to aid in any way they can. Farḍ kifāyah (كفاية) An obligation on the Muslim community as a whole, from which some are freed if others take it up, such as for jihad.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Fāsid (فاسد) _____, invalid/violable (in Islamic finance)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Fāsid (فاسد) Corrupt, invalid/violable (in Islamic finance). Fāsiq (فاسق) Anyone who has violated Islamic law; usually refers to one whose character has been corrupted (plural: "fāsiqūn"); in the Qur'an it refers to unbelievers who derided God for using similes and parables (in the Qur'an).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Fātiḥa (الفاتحة) The short, opening surah of the Qur'an, which begins with: "In the name of God, the _____, the Compassionate
Glossary of Islam.fact: Fātiḥa (الفاتحة) The short, opening surah of the Qur'an, which begins with: "In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Praise be to God, the Lord of the _____..." These words hold an important place in Muslim liturgies and forms the core of the salat
Glossary of Islam.fact: Praise be to God, the Lord of the Worlds..." These words hold an important place in Muslim liturgies and forms the core of the salat.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Fiqh (فقه) _____ built around the Shari'ah by custom (al-urf)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Fiqh (فقه) Jurisprudence built around the Shari'ah by custom (al-urf).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Literally: "deep understanding", refers to understanding the _____ laws
Glossary of Islam.fact: Literally: "deep understanding", refers to understanding the Islamic laws. Fī sabīl allāh (في سبيل الله) "For the sake of Allah"; a common Islamic expression for performing acts such as charity or jihad.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Fī sabīl allāh (في سبيل الله) "For the sake of Allah"; a common _____ expression for performing acts such as charity or jihad
Glossary of Islam.fact: Literally: "deep understanding", refers to understanding the Islamic laws. Fī sabīl allāh (في سبيل الله) "For the sake of Allah"; a common Islamic expression for performing acts such as charity or jihad.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Fir'aun (فرعون) _____: "Pharaoh"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Literally: "deep understanding", refers to understanding the Islamic laws. Fir'aun (فرعون) Literally: "Pharaoh".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: fitan) (فتنة) _____ or tribulation; also refers to any period of disorder, such as a civil war, or the period of time before the end of the world or any civil strife
Glossary of Islam.fact: fitan) (فتنة) Trial or tribulation; also refers to any period of disorder, such as a civil war, or the period of time before the end of the world or any civil strife. Fitnah: (n) temptation, discord, civil war, trial Fiṭrah (فطرة) Innate disposition towards virtue, knowledge, and beauty.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Fitnah: (n) temptation, discord, civil war, trial Fiṭrah (فطرة) _____ disposition towards virtue, knowledge, and beauty
Glossary of Islam.fact: Fitnah: (n) temptation, discord, civil war, trial Fiṭrah (فطرة) Innate disposition towards virtue, knowledge, and beauty.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Also the title of the 25th chapter (surah) of the Qu'ran (Al-_____)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Furqān (فرقان) The criterion (of right and wrong, true and false); for example, the Qur'an as furqan. Also the title of the 25th chapter (surah) of the Qu'ran (Al-Furqan).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Fuwaysiqah (فويسقة) _____, evil from the root fasaqa, meaning: "to deviate from the right way"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Fuwaysiqah (فويسقة) Vermin, evil from the root fasaqa, meaning: "to deviate from the right way".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ghaflah (غفلة) _____, forgetfulness of God, indifference Ghayb (غيب) The unseen, unknown
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ghaflah (غفلة) Heedlessness, forgetfulness of God, indifference Ghayb (غيب) The unseen, unknown.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ghanīmah (غنيمة) _____ of war, booty
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ghanīmah (غنيمة) Spoils of war, booty.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Gharar (غرر) _____ uncertainty; also "the sale of what is not present", such as fish not yet caught, crops not yet harvested
Glossary of Islam.fact: Gharar (غرر) Excessive uncertainty; also "the sale of what is not present", such as fish not yet caught, crops not yet harvested.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ghasbi (غصب) _____ unlawfully
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ghasbi (غصب) Possessed unlawfully.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ghāzi (غازى) (archaic) _____, "raider": used for whose who participated in war
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ghāzi (غازى) (archaic) Roughly, "raider": used for whose who participated in war.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ghusl (غسل) _____ ablution of the whole body (see: wudu)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ghasbi (غصب) Possessed unlawfully. Ghusl (غسل) Full ablution of the whole body (see: wudu).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḥadath aṣghar (أصغر) _____ ritual impurity
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥadath aṣghar (أصغر) Minor ritual impurity.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḥāfiẓ (حافظ) _____: "Memorizer or Protector"
Glossary of Islam.fact: (See also: the 99 names of God.) Ḥadīth (حديثḥadīth) plural ahādīth Literally: "speech"; a recorded saying or tradition of Muhammad validated by isnad; along with sira these comprise the Sunnah and reveal Shari'ah. Ḥāfiẓ (حافظ) Literally: "Memorizer or Protector".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḥājj (حاجّ) plural Ḥujjāj (حجّاج) and Ḥajīj (حجيج) A _____, one who has made the Hajj
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥājj (حاجّ) plural Ḥujjāj (حجّاج) and Ḥajīj (حجيج) A Pilgrim, one who has made the Hajj. Ḥajj (حجّ) and Ḥijjah (plurals Ḥijjāt (حجّات) and Ḥijaj (حجج)) One-time pilgrimage to Makkah (Mecca) during Dhu'l-Hijja.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḥajj (حجّ) and Ḥijjah (plurals Ḥijjāt (حجّات) and Ḥijaj (حجج)) One-time pilgrimage to _____ (Mecca) during Dhu'l-Hijja
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥajj (حجّ) and Ḥijjah (plurals Ḥijjāt (حجّات) and Ḥijaj (حجج)) One-time pilgrimage to Makkah (Mecca) during Dhu'l-Hijja.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Sunnis regard this as the fifth _____ of Islam
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sunnis regard this as the fifth Pillar of Islam.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: It is obligatory upon every _____ who is financially and physically capable of completing all necessary rites
Glossary of Islam.fact: It is obligatory upon every Muslim who is financially and physically capable of completing all necessary rites.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḥajj at-_____ʿ (التمتع) Performing ʿUmrah during the Hajj season, and on the Day of Tarwiah a pilgrim gets into the state of Ihram (sacred state) for Hajj
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥajj at-Tamattuʿ (التمتع) Performing ʿUmrah during the Hajj season, and on the Day of Tarwiah a pilgrim gets into the state of Ihram (sacred state) for Hajj.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Before making ʿ_____, one approaches the Miqat and declares their intention
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥajj at-Tamattuʿ (التمتع) Performing ʿUmrah during the Hajj season, and on the Day of Tarwiah a pilgrim gets into the state of Ihram (sacred state) for Hajj. Before making ʿUmrah, one approaches the Miqat and declares their intention.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḥajj al-Qirān (القران) _____, to declare an intention to perform both Hajj and 'Umrah together
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥajj al-Qirān (القران) At Miqat, to declare an intention to perform both Hajj and 'Umrah together. Ḥajj al-ʾIfrād (الإفراد) At Miqat, declare intention for Hajj only and maintain Ihram garments up to the Day of Sacrifice.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḥajj al-ʾIfrād (الإفراد) _____, declare intention for Hajj only and maintain Ihram garments up to the Day of Sacrifice
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥajj al-Qirān (القران) At Miqat, to declare an intention to perform both Hajj and 'Umrah together. Ḥajj al-ʾIfrād (الإفراد) At Miqat, declare intention for Hajj only and maintain Ihram garments up to the Day of Sacrifice.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: After throwing the _____ of Al-'Aqabah, getting hair shaved or cut that takes off his Ihram garments and sacrifices an animal
Glossary of Islam.fact: After throwing the Jamrah of Al-'Aqabah, getting hair shaved or cut that takes off his Ihram garments and sacrifices an animal.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḥākim (حاكم) A ruler's or governor's title; in some _____ states, a judge
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥākim (حاكم) A ruler's or governor's title; in some Muslim states, a judge.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḥākimīya (حاكمية) _____, governance
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥākimīya (حاكمية) Sovereignty, governance.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḥalāl (حلال) _____, permitted, good, beneficial, free from sin praiseworthy, honourable
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥalāl (حلال) Lawful, permitted, good, beneficial, free from sin praiseworthy, honourable.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Doing a halal action won't result in punishment in the _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: Doing a halal action won't result in punishment in the Hereafter.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḥalq (حلق) _____ of the head, particularly associated with pilgrimage to Makkah (Mecca)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥalq (حلق) Shaving of the head, particularly associated with pilgrimage to Makkah (Mecca).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḥanīf (حنيف) Pre-_____ non-Jewish or non-Christian monotheists
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥanīf (حنيف) Pre-Islamic non-Jewish or non-Christian monotheists.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḥaqq (حقّ) _____, reality, right, righteousness
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥaqq (حقّ) Truth, reality, right, righteousness.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: The English word algorithm is derived from the name of the inventor of algebra; similarly Arabic words like alchemy, alcohol, azimuth, nadir, zenith and _____, which mean the same as in English
Glossary of Islam.fact: The English word algorithm is derived from the name of the inventor of algebra; similarly Arabic words like alchemy, alcohol, azimuth, nadir, zenith and oasis, which mean the same as in English.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: The first day of the first Islamic year is _____ Muḥarram 1 (AH) and corresponds to 16 July 622 (CE)
Glossary of Islam.fact: The first day of the first Islamic year is 1 Muḥarram 1 (AH) and corresponds to 16 July 622 (CE).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Dār al-��Ahd (دَارُ الْعَهْدِ) _____'s relationship with its Christian tributary states
Glossary of Islam.fact: Dār al-��Ahd (دَارُ الْعَهْدِ) The Ottoman Empire's relationship with its Christian tributary states.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḥaram (حرم) _____ or sacred, used for land in Makkah (Mecca) and its surrounding areas.{[rp|96}} Ḥasan (حسن) Good, beautiful, admirable
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥaram (حرم) Sanctuary or sacred, used for land in Makkah (Mecca) and its surrounding areas.{[rp|96}} Ḥasan (حسن) Good, beautiful, admirable.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: ʾahwāʾ (أهواء)) _____ or egotistical desire; individual passion; impulsiveness
Glossary of Islam.fact: ʾahwāʾ (أهواء)) Vain or egotistical desire; individual passion; impulsiveness.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Hidāyah (هداية) _____ from God
Glossary of Islam.fact: Hidāyah (هداية) Guidance from God.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ḥijāb (حجاب) _____: "cover"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥijāb (حجاب) Literally: "cover". Hijra (الهجرة) Literally: "migration".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Hijra (الهجرة) _____: "migration"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ḥijāb (حجاب) Literally: "cover". Hijra (الهجرة) Literally: "migration".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Refers to the emigration of _____ and his followers from Makkah (Mecca) to Medina

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: It is part of the first _____ of Islam
Glossary of Islam.fact: It is part of the first Pillar of Islam.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: According to Islam, this is the message of all the _____, such as Ibrahim (Abraham), Musa (Moses), Isa (Jesus) and Muhammad
Glossary of Islam.fact: According to Islam, this is the message of all the Prophets, such as Ibrahim (Abraham), Musa (Moses), Isa (Jesus) and Muhammad.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Labbayka -llāhumma (لبّيكَ اللّهُم) "God, I obey you", a phrase said during _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: Labbayka -llāhumma (لبّيكَ اللّهُم) "God, I obey you", a phrase said during Hajj.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Laghw (لغو) _____, false, evil and vain talk
Glossary of Islam.fact: Laghw (لغو) Dirty, false, evil and vain talk.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Laʿnah (لعنة) _____, execration, or imprecation
Glossary of Islam.fact: Laʿnah (لعنة) Curse, execration, or imprecation.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Laylat al-Qadr (القدر) _____ of Power, towards the end of Ramadan, when Muhammad received the first revelation of the Qur'an
Glossary of Islam.fact: Laylat al-Qadr (القدر) The Night of Power, towards the end of Ramadan, when Muhammad received the first revelation of the Qur'an.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Madrasah (مدرسة) _____, university
Glossary of Islam.fact: Madhāhib (مذاهب), school of religious jurisprudence (fiqh), school of thought. Madrasah (مدرسة) School, university.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Mahdi (مهدي) _____: "a guide"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mahdi (مهدي) Literally: "a guide".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Maisir (ميسر) _____, game of chance
Glossary of Islam.fact: Maisir (ميسر) Gambling, game of chance.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: If a person commits the _____, he does not accumulate ithim but avoiding the Makhruh is rewarded with thawab
Glossary of Islam.fact: If a person commits the Makruh, he does not accumulate ithim but avoiding the Makhruh is rewarded with thawab.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Malāʾikah (ملائكة) Angels (_____: Malak)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Malāʾikah (ملائكة) Angels (Singular: Malak).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Belief in angels is one of the _____ of Islam and it is required for Muslims to believe in it
Glossary of Islam.fact: Belief in angels is one of the Five Pillars of Islam and it is required for Muslims to believe in it.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Mā malakat ʾaymānukum (أيمانكم) _____: "what your right hands possess"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mā malakat ʾaymānukum (أيمانكم) Literally: "what your right hands possess".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Manāsik (مناسك) The rules specifying the requirements of a legally valid _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: Manāsik (مناسك) The rules specifying the requirements of a legally valid Hajj.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Mandūb (مندوب) _____ or recommended
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mandūb (مندوب) Commendable or recommended.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: (See: halal, mustahabb) _____ (منهج) The methodology by which truth is reached
Glossary of Islam.fact: (See: halal, mustahabb) Manhaj (منهج) The methodology by which truth is reached.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: The doctrine of al-_____ wal-Mansukh (abrogation) of certain parts of the Qur'anic revelation by others
Glossary of Islam.fact: The doctrine of al-Nasikh wal-Mansukh (abrogation) of certain parts of the Qur'anic revelation by others.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Maʿrūf (معروف) _____ of the community
Glossary of Islam.fact: Maʿrūf (معروف) Consensus of the community.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: maqṣid (مقصد) Goals or purposes; such as the purposes of _____ law
Glossary of Islam.fact: maqṣid (مقصد) Goals or purposes; such as the purposes of Islamic law.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Mā shāʾa -llāh (ما شاء الله) "_____ has willed it", a common phrase expressing joy, praise
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mā shāʾa -llāh (ما شاء الله) "Allah has willed it", a common phrase expressing joy, praise.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Masīḥ (مسيح) The (_____) Messiah, prophet Isa (Jesus Christ)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Masīḥ (مسيح) The (Biblical) Messiah, prophet Isa (Jesus Christ).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: masājid, مساجد _____ of prayer; mosque
Glossary of Islam.fact: masājid, مساجد Place of prayer; mosque.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Masjid al-Ḥarām (الحرام) The mosque surrounding the Kaʿbah in _____ (Mecca)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Masjid al-Ḥarām (الحرام) The mosque surrounding the Kaʿbah in Makkah (Mecca).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Mawālī or mawālā (موالي) Non-_____
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mawālī or mawālā (موالي) Non-Arab Muslims.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: mawālin (موالٍ)] _____ or master
Glossary of Islam.fact: mawālin (موالٍ)] Protector or master.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Mawlānā (مولانا) _____ word meaning: "our master" (not literally)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mawlānā (مولانا) An Arabic word meaning: "our master" (not literally).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: The term is sometimes used to refer to _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: The term is sometimes used to refer to Rumi.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Maulvi (مولوی) An honorific _____ religious title often, but not exclusively, given to Muslim religious scholars or Ulama preceding their names
Glossary of Islam.fact: Maulvi (مولوی) An honorific Islamic religious title often, but not exclusively, given to Muslim religious scholars or Ulama preceding their names.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Mecca (مكّة _____) The holiest city in Islam
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mecca (مكّة Makkah) The holiest city in Islam.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Medina (مدينة Madīnah) _____: "city"; Medinat-un-Nabi means "the City of the Prophet." See Hijra (Islam) Mi'ād (معاد) The Resurrection; God will resurrect all of humankind to be judged
Glossary of Islam.fact: Medina (مدينة Madīnah) Literally: "city"; Medinat-un-Nabi means "the City of the Prophet." See Hijra (Islam) Mi'ād (معاد) The Resurrection; God will resurrect all of humankind to be judged.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Shi'as regard this as the fifth _____ of Islam
Glossary of Islam.fact: Shi'as regard this as the fifth Pillar of Islam.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Millah (مِلَّة) _____, millah means "religion," but it has only been used to refer to religions other than Islam, which is din
Glossary of Islam.fact: Millah (مِلَّة) In Arabic, millah means "religion," but it has only been used to refer to religions other than Islam, which is din.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Millet A _____ word meaning a nation, community, or a people
Glossary of Islam.fact: Millet A Turkish word meaning a nation, community, or a people.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: In an _____ state, "Ahl al Kitab" may continue to practice their former religion in a semi-autonomous community termed the millet
Glossary of Islam.fact: In an Islamic state, "Ahl al Kitab" may continue to practice their former religion in a semi-autonomous community termed the millet.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Minbar (منبر) A raised pulpit in the mosque where the _____ stands to deliver sermons
Glossary of Islam.fact: Minbar (منبر) A raised pulpit in the mosque where the Imam stands to deliver sermons.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Miʿrāj (المعراج) _____ to the Seven Heavens during the Night Journey (See also: Al-Isra)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Miʿrāj (المعراج) The Ascension to the Seven Heavens during the Night Journey (See also: Al-Isra).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Mosque (مسجد) A _____ place of worship (see: masjid)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mosque (مسجد) A Muslim place of worship (see: masjid).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Muʿawwidhatayn (المعوذتين) _____-Falaq and an-Nas, the "Surahs of refuge", should be said to relieve suffering (also to protect from Black Magic)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Muʿawwidhatayn (المعوذتين) Suras Al-Falaq and an-Nas, the "Surahs of refuge", should be said to relieve suffering (also to protect from Black Magic).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Mubāḥ (مباح) _____: "permissible"; neither forbidden nor commended, neutral
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mubāḥ (مباح) Literally: "permissible"; neither forbidden nor commended, neutral.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Mufassir (مُفسّر) _____ exegete of the Qur'an
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mufassir (مُفسّر) Qualified exegete of the Qur'an.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Muftī (مفتى) _____ scholar who is an interpreter or expounder of Islamic law (Shari'ah), capable of issuing fatawa (plural of fatwa)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Muftī (مفتى) An Islamic scholar who is an interpreter or expounder of Islamic law (Shari'ah), capable of issuing fatawa (plural of fatwa).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Muḥkamāt _____ verses of the Qur'an
Glossary of Islam.fact: Muḥkamāt Unequivocal verses of the Qur'an.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Muḥammadun rasūl allāh (محمدٌ رسول الله) "_____ is the messenger of God." This statement is the second part of the first Pillar of Islam, and it is the second most important statement in Islam
Glossary of Islam.fact: Muḥammadun rasūl allāh (محمدٌ رسول الله) "Muhammad is the messenger of God." This statement is the second part of the first Pillar of Islam, and it is the second most important statement in Islam.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: It forms the second half of the _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: It forms the second half of the Shahada.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Muhājirūn (مهاجرون) The first _____ that accompanied Muhammad when he traveled to Medina
Glossary of Islam.fact: Muhājirūn (مهاجرون) The first Muslims that accompanied Muhammad when he traveled to Medina.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Mullah (ملا) Refers to _____ clergy
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mullah (ملا) Refers to Islamic clergy. Ideally, they should have studied the Qur'an, Islamic traditions (hadith), and Islamic law (fiqh).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ideally, they should have studied the Qur'an, _____ traditions (hadith), and Islamic law (fiqh)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mullah (ملا) Refers to Islamic clergy. Ideally, they should have studied the Qur'an, Islamic traditions (hadith), and Islamic law (fiqh).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Muʾmin (مؤمن) A _____ who observes the commandments of the Qur'an
Glossary of Islam.fact: Muʾmin (مؤمن) A Muslim who observes the commandments of the Qur'an.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Murābaḥah ( مرابحة) A type of _____'ah-compliant mortgage (see Ijara)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Murābaḥah ( مرابحة) A type of Shari'ah-compliant mortgage (see Ijara).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Murshid (مرشد) A _____ teacher
Glossary of Islam.fact: Murshid (مرشد) A Sufi teacher.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Murtadd (مرتد), a female apostate is _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: Murtadd (مرتد), a female apostate is Murtaddah Apostate.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Muslim (مسلم) A follower of the religion of Islam, one who submits their will to God (_____)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Muslim (مسلم) A follower of the religion of Islam, one who submits their will to God (Allah).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Mustaḥabb (مستحبّ) _____ or recommended
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mustaḥabb (مستحبّ) Commendable or recommended.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Mutʿah (متعة) _____: "enjoyment"; compensation paid to a divorced woman; when used in the phrase nikāḥ al-mutʿah (المتعة) it refers to the temporary marriage that is practiced in Twelver Shi'a Islam
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mutʿah (متعة) Literally: "enjoyment"; compensation paid to a divorced woman; when used in the phrase nikāḥ al-mutʿah (المتعة) it refers to the temporary marriage that is practiced in Twelver Shi'a Islam.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Mutashābihāt (متشابهات) _____ verses of Qur'an
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mutashābihāt (متشابهات) Equivocal verses of Qur'an.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Muṭawwaʿūn (مطوّعون) (مطوعين) (singular muṭawwaʿ) _____ police
Glossary of Islam.fact: Muṭawwaʿ (مطوّع) plural muṭawwaʿūn (مطوّعون) A religious man in certain regions, a volunteer teacher. Muṭawwaʿūn (مطوّعون) (مطوعين) (singular muṭawwaʿ) Religious police.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Mutawātir (متواتر) "_____ upon", used to describe hadith that were narrated by many witnesses through different narration chains (isnads) leading back to Muhammad
Glossary of Islam.fact: Mutawātir (متواتر) "Agreed upon", used to describe hadith that were narrated by many witnesses through different narration chains (isnads) leading back to Muhammad.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: In the _____ context, a Nabi is a man sent by God to give guidance to man, but not given scripture
Glossary of Islam.fact: In the Islamic context, a Nabi is a man sent by God to give guidance to man, but not given scripture.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: The Prophet Abraham was a _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: In the Islamic context, a Nabi is a man sent by God to give guidance to man, but not given scripture. The Prophet Abraham was a Nabi.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: This is in contrast to a Rasul, or _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: This is in contrast to a Rasul, or Messenger.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Nafs (النفس) _____, the lower self, the ego/id
Glossary of Islam.fact: Nafs (النفس) Soul, the lower self, the ego/id.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Nakīr and _____ (منكر) Two angels who test the faith of the dead in their graves
Glossary of Islam.fact: Nakīr and Munkar (منكر) Two angels who test the faith of the dead in their graves.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Namāz (نماز) _____ in Turkish and Persian language
Glossary of Islam.fact: Namāz (نماز) Ritual Prayer in Turkish and Persian language.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Nashīd (نشيد) A popular type of a cappella in _____ culture
Glossary of Islam.fact: Nashīd (نشيد) A popular type of a cappella in Islamic culture.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Naskh (نسخ) The doctrine of al-Nasikh wal-_____ (abrogation) of certain parts of the Qur'anic revelation by others
Glossary of Islam.fact: Naskh (نسخ) The doctrine of al-Nasikh wal-Mansukh (abrogation) of certain parts of the Qur'anic revelation by others. The principle is mentioned in the Qur'an (2:106), see mansukh.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Nifās (نفاس) The bleeding after childbirth (see _____)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Nifās (نفاس) The bleeding after childbirth (see Haid).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Nifāq (نفاق) _____; dishonesty; hypocrisy
Glossary of Islam.fact: Nifāq (نفاق) Falsehood; dishonesty; hypocrisy.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Nihāļ (نحال) _____ name meaning: "joyful." Nikāḥ (النكاح) The matrimonial contract between a bride and bridegroom within an Islamic marriage
Glossary of Islam.fact: Nihāļ (نحال) An Arabic name meaning: "joyful." Nikāḥ (النكاح) The matrimonial contract between a bride and bridegroom within an Islamic marriage.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Shi'a regard this as the third _____ of Islam
Glossary of Islam.fact: Shi'a regard this as the third Pillar of Islam.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Nūr (نور) Light, more theological connoted than daw', the proper term for light in _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: Nūr (نور) Light, more theological connoted than daw', the proper term for light in Arabic.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Nur is often associated with benevolence, such as the Light of _____ and angels of mercy as created from nur
Glossary of Islam.fact: Nur is often associated with benevolence, such as the Light of Muhammad and angels of mercy as created from nur.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: The term is closely associated with nar, which denotes the burning light of fire, often associated with fierce forces, like the angels of punishment, demons and _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: The term is closely associated with nar, which denotes the burning light of fire, often associated with fierce forces, like the angels of punishment, demons and Hell.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: In some circles and _____ writings, Sufis regard PBUH to signify "Peace and Blessings Upon Him" (the Rasul or Messenger of Allah)
Glossary of Islam.fact: In some circles and English writings, Sufis regard PBUH to signify "Peace and Blessings Upon Him" (the Rasul or Messenger of Allah). These are the primary English explications of the P.B.U.H. The Arabic version is S.A.W. Qadar (قدر) Predestination.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: These are the primary _____ explications of the P.B.U.H
Glossary of Islam.fact: In some circles and English writings, Sufis regard PBUH to signify "Peace and Blessings Upon Him" (the Rasul or Messenger of Allah). These are the primary English explications of the P.B.U.H. The Arabic version is S.A.W. Qadar (قدر) Predestination.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Qāḍī (قاضي) A Judge of _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: Qāḍī (قاضي) A Judge of Islamic Law.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Qalb (قلب) Heart, considered the center of the self in _____ anthropology
Glossary of Islam.fact: Qāḍī (قاضي) A Judge of Islamic Law. Qalb (قلب) Heart, considered the center of the self in Islamic anthropology.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Qiblah (قبلة) The direction _____ face during prayer, which is towards the Ka'aba in Makkah (Mecca)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Qiblah (قبلة) The direction Muslims face during prayer, which is towards the Ka'aba in Makkah (Mecca).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Qitāl fī sabīl allāh ( قتال في سبيل الله) _____ in the cause of Allah
Glossary of Islam.fact: Qitāl fī sabīl allāh ( قتال في سبيل الله) Fight in the cause of Allah.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Qiyāmah (قيامة) _____; return of the dead for the Day of Judgment
Glossary of Islam.fact: Qiyāmah (قيامة) Resurrection; return of the dead for the Day of Judgment.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Qiṣāṣ (قصاص) _____ retribution, a fine for murder if the heirs forgive the perpetrator
Glossary of Islam.fact: Qiṣāṣ (قصاص) Equitable retribution, a fine for murder if the heirs forgive the perpetrator.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Qiyās (القياس) _____ – foundation of legal reasoning and thus fiqh
Glossary of Islam.fact: Qiyās (القياس) Analogy – foundation of legal reasoning and thus fiqh.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Qudsī (قدسي) _____ of a hadith that is believed to be narrated by Muhammad from God
Glossary of Islam.fact: Qudsī (قدسي) Classification of a hadith that is believed to be narrated by Muhammad from God.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Qurbah (قربة) _____ to God, associated with Sufism
Glossary of Islam.fact: Qurbah (قربة) Closeness to God, associated with Sufism.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: R. A., raḍiya -llāhu ʿanhu (عنه) "_____ be pleased with him"
Glossary of Islam.fact: R. A., raḍiya -llāhu ʿanhu (عنه) "May Allah be pleased with him".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Raḥmān (رحمن) _____; Ar-Rahman (الرحمن) means: "The Most Merciful"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Raḥmān (رحمن) Merciful; Ar-Rahman (الرحمن) means: "The Most Merciful".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Raḥīm (رحيم) _____; Ar-Rahim (الرحيم) means "The Most Compassionate", as seen in the Basmala ("Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm")
Glossary of Islam.fact: Raḥīm (رحيم) Compassionate; Ar-Rahim (الرحيم) means "The Most Compassionate", as seen in the Basmala ("Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm").

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Raḥimaḥullāh (رحمه الله) "_____ have mercy on him"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Raḥimaḥullāh (رحمه الله) "May Allah have mercy on him".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Usually used after mentioning the companions of _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: Usually used after mentioning the companions of Muhammad.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Raḥmatullāh (رحمة الله) _____ of Allah
Glossary of Islam.fact: Raḥimaḥullāh (رحمه الله) "May Allah have mercy on him". Raḥmatullāh (رحمة الله) Mercy of Allah.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Sometimes used as an alternative to _____ after mentioning a righteous person by saying, "rahmatullahi ʿilayh" (رحمة الله علیه)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sometimes used as an alternative to Rahimahullah after mentioning a righteous person by saying, "rahmatullahi ʿilayh" (رحمة الله علیه).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: English: "_____ of Allah be upon him/her"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Raḥmatullāh (رحمة الله) Mercy of Allah. English: "Mercy of Allah be upon him/her".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Rajm (رجم) _____ or banishment, used as an epithet for devils in some Islamic prayers
Glossary of Islam.fact: Rajm (رجم) Stoning or banishment, used as an epithet for devils in some Islamic prayers.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Rakʿah (ركعة) One unit of _____ prayer, or Salat
Glossary of Islam.fact: Rajm (رجم) Stoning or banishment, used as an epithet for devils in some Islamic prayers. Rakʿah (ركعة) One unit of Islamic prayer, or Salat.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Spelt as _____, Ramadhan, or Ramathan as well
Glossary of Islam.fact: Spelt as Ramzaan, Ramadhan, or Ramathan as well.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Rāshidūn (راشدون) _____ consider the first four caliphs as the "orthodox" or "rightly guided" caliphs
Glossary of Islam.fact: Rāshidūn (راشدون) Sunnis consider the first four caliphs as the "orthodox" or "rightly guided" caliphs.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: They were _____, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali
Glossary of Islam.fact: They were Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Rasūl (رسول) _____; unlike prophets (Nabi), messengers are given scripture
Glossary of Islam.fact: Rasūl (رسول) Messenger; unlike prophets (Nabi), messengers are given scripture. Musa (Moses), Dawud (David), Isa (Jesus) and Muhammed are considered messengers.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Musa (Moses), Dawud (David), Isa (Jesus) and _____ are considered messengers
Glossary of Islam.fact: Musa (Moses), Dawud (David), Isa (Jesus) and Muhammed are considered messengers.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Riba (ربا) _____, the charging and paying of which is forbidden by the Qur'an
Glossary of Islam.fact: Riba (ربا) Interest, the charging and paying of which is forbidden by the Qur'an.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Riddah (ردة) _____, in which a person abandons Islam for another faith or no faith at all
Glossary of Islam.fact: Riddah (ردة) Apostasy, in which a person abandons Islam for another faith or no faith at all.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Risālah (رِسَالَة) _____: "message" or "letter"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Risālah (رِسَالَة) Literally: "message" or "letter".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Rūḥ (روح) _____; the divine breath which God blew into the clay of Adam
Glossary of Islam.fact: Rūḥ (روح) Spirit; the divine breath which God blew into the clay of Adam.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Rukn (ركن) plural ʾArkān (أركان) "What is inevitable", one of the _____ pillars of Islam
Glossary of Islam.fact: Rukn (ركن) plural ʾArkān (أركان) "What is inevitable", one of the Five pillars of Islam.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ṣabr (صبر) _____, endurance, self-restraint
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ṣabr (صبر) Patience, endurance, self-restraint.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ṣadaqah (صدقة) _____; voluntary alms above the amount for zakat
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ṣadaqah (صدقة) Charity; voluntary alms above the amount for zakat.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ṣāḥib) (صاحب) _____ of Muhammad
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ṣāḥib) (صاحب) Companions of Muhammad. A list of the best-known Companions can be found at the article: List of companions of Muhammad.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: A list of the best-known _____ can be found at the article: List of companions of Muhammad
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ṣāḥib) (صاحب) Companions of Muhammad. A list of the best-known Companions can be found at the article: List of companions of Muhammad.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ṣāḥīḥ (صحيح) "_____ in isnad." A technical attribute applied to the "isnad" of a hadith
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ṣāḥīḥ (صحيح) "Sound in isnad." A technical attribute applied to the "isnad" of a hadith.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Sakīnah (سكينة) _____ "tranquility" or "peace" which descends upon a person when the Qur'an is recited
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sakīnah (سكينة) Divine "tranquility" or "peace" which descends upon a person when the Qur'an is recited.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Salaf (الصالح) (_____) predecessors/ancestors
Glossary of Islam.fact: Salaf (الصالح) (Righteous) predecessors/ancestors.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: In Islam, Salaf is generally used to refer to the first three generations of _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: In Islam, Salaf is generally used to refer to the first three generations of Muslims. Anyone who died after this is one of the khalaf, or "latter-day Muslims".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Anyone who died after this is one of the khalaf, or "latter-day _____"
Glossary of Islam.fact: In Islam, Salaf is generally used to refer to the first three generations of Muslims. Anyone who died after this is one of the khalaf, or "latter-day Muslims".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Salafism A reform movement, basing _____ teachings on Qur'an and Sunnah alone
Glossary of Islam.fact: Salafism A reform movement, basing Islamic teachings on Qur'an and Sunnah alone.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Contrary to _____, it disregards former established consensus and the opinions of the Sahaba
Glossary of Islam.fact: Contrary to Classical Sunnism, it disregards former set up consensus and the opinions of the Sahaba.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Sunnis regard this as the second _____ of Islam
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sunnis regard this as the second Pillar of Islam.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Salaat al-_____ for guidance is done in conjunction with two rakaahs of supererogatory prayer
Glossary of Islam.fact: Salaat al-Istikharah Prayer for guidance is done in conjunction with two rakaahs of supererogatory prayer.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Salām (سلام) _____ (see sulh)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Salām (سلام) Peace (see sulh). Sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (سلم) "May Allah bless him and grant him peace." The expression is often used after Muhammad's name.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (سلم) "_____ bless him and grant him peace." The expression is often used after Muhammad's name
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (سلم) "May Allah bless him and grant him peace." The expression is often used after Muhammad's name.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ṣamad (صمد) _____, absolute; Muslims believe Allah is "The Eternal." Salsabīl (سلسبيل) A river in heaven (al-firdaus)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ṣamad (صمد) Eternal, absolute; Muslims believe Allah is "The Eternal." Salsabīl (سلسبيل) A river in heaven (al-firdaus).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: (or S.A.W.S.) "_____ alayhi wa sallam" (سلم)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (سلم) "May Allah bless him and grant him peace." The expression is often used after Muhammad's name. (or S.A.W.S.) "Sallallahu alayhi wa sallam" (سلم).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ṣawm (صَوم) _____ during the month of Ramadan
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ṣawm (صَوم) Fasting during the month of Ramadan.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: The word sawm is derived from the _____ word sawmo
Glossary of Islam.fact: The word sawm is derived from the Syriac word sawmo.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Sayyid (سيّد, also spelled _____) In everyday usage, it is equivalent to 'Mr.'
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sayyid (سيّد, also spelled Seyed) In everyday usage, it is equivalent to 'Mr.'.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Also refers to a descendant of a relative of _____, usually via Husayn
Glossary of Islam.fact: Also refers to a descendant of a relative of Muhammad, usually via Husayn.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Seghatoleslam (ثقة الاسلام),(ثقت الاسلام) "_____ of Islam", a title given to religious scholars in Shi'a sect
Glossary of Islam.fact: Seghatoleslam (ثقة الاسلام),(ثقت الاسلام) "Trustworthy of Islam", a title given to religious scholars in Shi'a sect.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Sema Refers to some of the ceremonies used by various _____ orders
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sema Refers to some of the ceremonies used by various Sufi orders.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Muhammad is the messenger of _____.")
Glossary of Islam.fact: Shahādah (الشهادة) The testimony of faith: "La ilaha illa Allah. Muhammad is the messenger of Allah.").

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Formal conversion to Islam is done by the recitation of the _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: Formal conversion to Islam is done by the recitation of the Shahada.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Sunnis regard this as the first _____ of Islam, while Shi'as also add an optional third statement, "Ali is the wali of God" ("Wa ʿaliyyun waliyyu llāh")
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sunnis regard this as the first Pillar of Islam, while Shi'as also add an optional third statement, "Ali is the wali of God" ("Wa ʿaliyyun waliyyu llāh").

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: It also may be used as a synonym for the term _____'hād, meaning martyrdom
Glossary of Islam.fact: It also may be used as a synonym for the term Istish'hād, meaning martyrdom.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: shuhadāʾ (شهداء) _____, martyr
Glossary of Islam.fact: shuhadāʾ (شهداء) Witness, martyr.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Usually refers to a person killed whilst fighting in "jihād fī sabīl Allāh" (jihad for the sake of _____)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Usually refers to a person killed whilst fighting in "jihād fī sabīl Allāh" (jihad for the sake of Allah).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Often used in modern times for deaths in a political cause (including victims of soldiers, deaths in battle, etc.) which are viewed by some _____ as a spiritual cause, not just as a political cause
Glossary of Islam.fact: Often used in modern times for deaths in a political cause (including victims of soldiers, deaths in battle, etc.) which are viewed by some Muslims as a spiritual cause, not just as a political cause.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Shaykh (شيخ) A spiritual master, _____ clergy
Glossary of Islam.fact: Often used in modern times for deaths in a political cause (including victims of soldiers, deaths in battle, etc.) which are viewed by some Muslims as a spiritual cause, not just as a political cause. Shaykh (شيخ) A spiritual master, Muslim clergy.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Sharīʿah (الشريعة) "The path to a watering hole"; _____ law; the eternal ethical code and moral code based on the Qur'an, Sunnah, Ijma, and Qiyas; basis of Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sharīʿah (الشريعة) "The path to a watering hole"; Islamic law; the eternal ethical code and moral code based on the Qur'an, Sunnah, Ijma, and Qiyas; basis of Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Sharīf (شريف) A title bestowed upon the descendants of _____ through Hasan, the son of his daughter Fatima Zahra and son-in-law Ali ibn Abi Talib
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sharīf (شريف) A title bestowed upon the descendants of Muhammad through Hasan, the son of his daughter Fatima Zahra and son-in-law Ali ibn Abi Talib.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: With the article Al- it designates _____ (Iblis) in particular
Glossary of Islam.fact: With the article Al- it designates Satan (Iblis) in particular.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Shīʿah (الشيعة) A branch of Islam who believe in _____ and his sons (Hassan and Hussayn) as the custodians of Islam by the will of Muhammed
Glossary of Islam.fact: Shīʿah (الشيعة) A branch of Islam who believe in Imam Ali and his sons (Hassan and Hussayn) as the custodians of Islam by the will of Muhammed.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Shirk (شرك) _____; polytheism; the sin of believing in any divinity except God and of associating other gods with God
Glossary of Islam.fact: Shirk (شرك) Idolatry; polytheism; the sin of believing in any divinity except God and of associating other gods with God.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Majlis ash-shūrā (الشورى) An advisory council in a _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: Majlis ash-shūrā (الشورى) An advisory council in a Caliphate.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Sidrat al-_____ (المنتهى) A lotus tree that marks the end of the seventh heaven, the boundary where no creation can pass
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sidrat al-Muntaha (المنتهى) A lotus tree that marks the end of the seventh heaven, the boundary where no creation can pass.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Sīrah (السيرة) Life or biography of _____; his moral example – along with hadith, this comprises the sunnah
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sīrah (السيرة) Life or biography of Muhammad; his moral example – along with hadith, this comprises the sunnah.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: aṣ-Ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm ( المستقيم) _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: aṣ-Ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm ( المستقيم) The Straight Path.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Subḥānahu wa taʿāla (تعالى) (abbreviated as '_____ text'S.W.T.) An expression used following the written name or vocalization of Allah in Arabic, meaning "highly praised and glorified is He"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Subḥānahu wa taʿāla (تعالى) (abbreviated as 'Italic text'S.W.T.) An expression used following the written name or vocalization of Allah in Arabic, meaning "highly praised and glorified is He".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Subḥān allāh (سبحان الله) "_____ to God" – this phrase is often used when praising God or exclaiming awe at His attributes, bounties, or creation
Glossary of Islam.fact: Subḥān allāh (سبحان الله) "Glory to God" – this phrase is often used when praising God or exclaiming awe at His attributes, bounties, or creation.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ṣūfī (صوفي) A _____ mystic; see: Sufism (tasawwuf)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ṣūfī (صوفي) A Muslim mystic; see: Sufism (tasawwuf). Suḥūr (سحور) The meal eaten by fasting Muslims just before dawn.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Suḥūr (سحور) The meal eaten by fasting _____ just before dawn
Glossary of Islam.fact: Suḥūr (سحور) The meal eaten by fasting Muslims just before dawn.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Sujūd (سجود) _____ down, a position of salat
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sujūd (سجود) Kneeling down, a position of salat.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ṣukūk (صكوك) _____ that generates revenue from sales, profits, or leases rather than interest
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ṣukūk (صكوك) Bond that generates revenue from sales, profits, or leases rather than interest.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Sunnah (السنّة) or sunnat an-Nabī (سنّة النبي) The "path" or "example" of _____, i.e., what he did or said or agreed to during his life
Glossary of Islam.fact: Sunnah (السنّة) or sunnat an-Nabī (سنّة النبي) The "path" or "example" of Muhammad, i.e., what he did or said or agreed to during his life.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: He is considered by _____ to be the best human moral example
Glossary of Islam.fact: He is considered by Muslims to be the best human moral example.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: The word Sunni comes from the word Sunnah (Arabic: سنة), which refers to the words and actions or example of the _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: The word Sunni comes from the word Sunnah (Arabic: سنة), which refers to the words and actions or example of the Islamic Prophet Muhammad.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Tābiʿīn (التابعون) _____ of the Ṣaḥābah
Glossary of Islam.fact: Tābiʿīn (التابعون) Followers of the Ṣaḥābah.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Tafsīr (تفسير) _____, particularly such commentary on the Qur'an
Glossary of Islam.fact: Tafsīr (تفسير) Exegesis, particularly such commentary on the Qur'an.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ṭāghūt (طاغوت) (taghout) "_____ god" or idol; also tyranny
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ṭāghūt (طاغوت) (taghout) "False god" or idol; also tyranny.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Tahajjud (تهجُّد) _____ (supererogatory), late-night (pre-dawn) prayer
Glossary of Islam.fact: Tahajjud (تهجُّد) Optional (supererogatory), late-night (pre-dawn) prayer.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ṭahārah (طهارة) _____ from ritual impurities by means of wudu or ghusl
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ṭahārah (طهارة) Purification from ritual impurities by means of wudu or ghusl.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ṭāhir (طاهر) _____, ritually clean
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ṭāhir (طاهر) Pure, ritually clean.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Tahlīl (تهليل) _____ the formula of faith: "Lā ilāha illā -llāh", English: "There is no god but God"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Tahlīl (تهليل) Uttering the formula of faith: "Lā ilāha illā -llāh", English: "There is no god but God".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Forms the first half of the _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: Forms the first half of the Shahada.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Tahmid (تحميد) To praise Allah or to say, "_____"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Tahmid (تحميد) To praise Allah or to say, "Alhamdillah".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: It derives from the same root as _____, mahmud and hamid (hmd) which means praise in Arabic
Glossary of Islam.fact: It derives from the same root as Muhammad, mahmud and hamid (hmd) which means praise in Arabic.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Taḥnīk (تحنيك) _____ ceremony of touching the lips of a newborn baby with honey, sweet juice or pressed dates
Glossary of Islam.fact: Taḥnīk (تحنيك) An Islamic ceremony of touching the lips of a newborn baby with honey, sweet juice or pressed dates.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Taḥrīf (تحريف) _____, forgery
Glossary of Islam.fact: Taḥrīf (تحريف) Corruption, forgery.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Muslims believe the _____ (Injil) were corrupted but the Qur'an is in its original form
Glossary of Islam.fact: Muslims believe the Bible Scriptures (Injil) were corrupted but the Qur'an is in its original form.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Tajdīd (تجديد) _____: "to make new" in the present tense
Glossary of Islam.fact: Tajdīd (تجديد) Literally: "to make new" in the present tense.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Takāful ( التكافل) Based on Shari'ah (_____ law), it is a form of mutual insurance
Glossary of Islam.fact: Takāful ( التكافل) Based on Shari'ah (Islamic law), it is a form of mutual insurance.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Takbīr (تكبير) A proclamation of the greatness of Allah; a _____ invocation
Glossary of Islam.fact: Takbīr (تكبير) A proclamation of the greatness of Allah; a Muslim invocation. Takfīr (تكفير) Declaration of an individual or group of previously considered Muslim as kaffir.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Takfīr (تكفير) _____ of an individual or group of previously considered Muslim as kaffir
Glossary of Islam.fact: Takfīr (تكفير) Declaration of an individual or group of previously considered Muslim as kaffir.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Taqlīd (تقليد) To follow the scholarly opinion of one of the four Imams (madhhab) of _____ (fiqh)
Glossary of Islam.fact: Taqlīd (تقليد) To follow the scholarly opinion of one of the four Imams (madhhab) of Islamic Jurisprudence (fiqh).

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Taqīyyah (تقيّة) "_____", that one is allowed to hide his true beliefs in certain circumstances or to lie to save himself from being killed or harmed
Glossary of Islam.fact: Taqīyyah (تقيّة) "Precaution", that one is allowed to hide his true beliefs in certain circumstances or to lie to save himself from being killed or harmed.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Taqwa (تقوى) _____; goodness; piety
Glossary of Islam.fact: Taqwa (تقوى) Righteousness; goodness; piety.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Taqwa is taken from the verbe _____, which means "avoiding", fearing the punishment from Allah for committing sins
Glossary of Islam.fact: Taqwa is taken from the verbe Ittaqua, which means "avoiding", fearing the punishment from Allah for committing sins.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: It is piety obtained by fearing the punishment of _____
Glossary of Islam.fact: Taqwa is taken from the verbe Ittaqua, which means "avoiding", fearing the punishment from Allah for committing sins. It is piety obtained by fearing the punishment of Allah.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Tarāwīḥ (تراويح) Extra prayers in _____ after the Isha prayer
Glossary of Islam.fact: Tarāwīḥ (تراويح) Extra prayers in Ramadan after the Isha prayer.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Tarkīb (تَرْكِيب) The study of _____ grammar issued from the Qur'an
Glossary of Islam.fact: Tarkīb (تَرْكِيب) The study of Arabic grammar issued from the Qur'an.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ṭarīqah (طريقة) A _____ religious order, particularly a Sufi order
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ṭarīqah (طريقة) A Muslim religious order, particularly a Sufi order.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Taṣawwuf (التصوّف) or _____īḥ (تسبيح) Uttering the phrase: "Subhan Allah", English: "Glory be to Allah"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Taṣawwuf (التصوّف) or Sufism Tasbīḥ (تسبيح) Uttering the phrase: "Subhan Allah", English: "Glory be to Allah".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Tashkīl (تشكيل) _____: "to form" or "arrange"
Glossary of Islam.fact: Tashkīl (تشكيل) Literally: "to form" or "arrange".

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Vocalization of _____ text by means of diacritical marks
Glossary of Islam.fact: Vocalization of Arabic text by means of diacritical marks. Forms an integral part of the Arabic writing system.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Forms an integral part of the _____ writing system
Glossary of Islam.fact: Vocalization of Arabic text by means of diacritical marks. Forms an integral part of the Arabic writing system.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Taslīm (تسليم) _____ at the end of prayer
Glossary of Islam.fact: Taslīm (تسليم) Salutation at the end of prayer.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Taṭbīr (تطبير) Shi'a _____ ceremony of self-flagellation by hitting the head with a sword
Glossary of Islam.fact: Taṭbīr (تطبير) Shi'a Ashura ceremony of self-flagellation by hitting the head with a sword.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Tawakkul (توکل) _____ reliance on Allah
Glossary of Islam.fact: Tawakkul (توکل) Total reliance on Allah.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Tawassul (توسُّل) _____ through the medium and intercession of another person
Glossary of Islam.fact: Tawassul (توسُّل) Asking Allah Almighty through the medium and intercession of another person.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations
Glossary of Islam.question: Ṭawāf (طواف) _____ the Ka'bah during Hajj
Glossary of Islam.fact: Ṭawāf (طواف) Circumambulating the Ka'bah during Hajj.

Glossary of Islam.subject: International Relations

Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: The squadrons involved were VA-34 "Blue Blasters" (from USS America) and VA-55 "Warhorses" (from USS Coral Sea).

Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: On 19 October 1987, Intruders of VA-145 operating from USS Ranger attacked Iranian oil platforms during Operation Nimble Archer.

Grumman A-6 Intruder.subject: International Relations

Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: On 19 April 1988, VA-95 Intruders operating from USS Enterprise sank the Iranian frigate, Sahand and severely damaged the Iranian frigate, Sabalan during Operation Praying Mantis.

Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: They were also the U.S. Navy's primary strike platform for delivering laser-guided bombs. The U.S. Navy operated them from the aircraft carriers USS Saratoga, USS John F. Kennedy, USS Midway, USS Ranger, USS America and USS Theodore Roosevelt, while U.S. Marine Corps A-6s operated ashore, primarily from Shaikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain.

Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: Three A-6s were shot down in combat by SAMs and AAA.

Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: Following the Gulf War, Intruders were used to patrol the no-fly zone in Iraq and provided air support for U.S. Marines during Operation Restore Hope in Somalia.

Grumman A-6 Intruder.subject: International Relations

Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: The last A-6E Intruder left U.S. Marine Corps service on 28 April 1993.

Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: The last A-6E Intruder left U.S. Marine Corps service on 28 April 1993.

Grumman A-6 Intruder.subject: International Relations

Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: Navy A-6s saw further duty over Bosnia in 1994.

Grumman A-6 Intruder.subject: International Relations

Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: On 4 June 1996, during RIMPAC a US Navy A-6E performing the unusual target towing task to train Japanese Navy air defense crews was mistakenly engaged and shot down by the Japanese destroyer JS Yūgiri with its Phalanx CIWS gun.

Grumman A-6 Intruder.subject: International Relations

Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: The A-6 was intended to be replaced by the McDonnell Douglas A-12 Avenger II, but that program was canceled due to cost overruns.

Grumman A-6 Intruder.subject: International Relations
Grumman A-6 Intruder.question: The last Intruders were retired on 28 February _____
Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: The last Intruders were retired on 28 February 1997.

Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: At the time of retirement, several retired A-6 airframes were awaiting rewinging at the Northrop Grumman facility at St.

Grumman A-6 Intruder.subject: International Relations
Grumman A-6 Intruder.question: Augustine Airport, _____; these were later sunk off the coast of St
Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: Augustine Airport, Florida; these were later sunk off the coast of St.

Grumman A-6 Intruder.subject: International Relations

Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: Between 1968 and 1977, several Intruder squadrons operated A-6Bs alongside their regular A-6As.

Grumman A-6 Intruder.subject: International Relations
Grumman A-6 Intruder.question: They were fitted with a "Trails/_____-sensor" (TRIM) pod in the fuselage for FLIR and low-light TV cameras, as well as a "Black Crow" engine ignition detection system
Grumman A-6 Intruder.fact: They were fitted with a "Trails/Roads Interdiction Multi-sensor" (TRIM) pod in the fuselage for FLIR and low-light TV cameras, as well as a "Black Crow" engine ignition detection system.

Grumman A-6 Intruder.subject: International Relations
